iconicAnchor.label: Couture toiles as three-dimensional working sketches
iconicAnchor.creatorOrTradition: Haute couture ateliers and dressmaking practice
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: The Met explains how inexpensive muslin toiles enable draping, tailoring, experimentation, fit refinement, and the translation of a design idea into material form.

sources.title: Manus x Machina exhibition galleries: Toiles
supports: Toiles are preliminary three-dimensional sketches used for draping, tailoring, experimentation, and refinements in fit.
Atelier flou and atelier tailleur practices support showing both dress-form work and flat-pattern development.

sources.title: I Do: Yohji Yamamoto wedding dress
supports: Visible grain lines, tucks, darts, stitches, and dressmaker's marks make the draping process legible.
Provisional muslin can communicate the energy of a sketch while retaining careful atelier finish.

bundledReferenceRationale: Excellent single-image set. The lead clearly teaches illustrated, atelier signal, craft signal, fabric, retains its identity at card scale, and shows no visible anti-cue, integrity failure, or confusing overlap with neighboring styles. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/atelier-process/generated-lead.jpg. No support image is needed because the lead carries the direction without filler.
